en: The Sūtra on the King of Mantras for Eradicating Karmic Obstructions Spoken by the Buddha, in one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Yijing by Imperial Command.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavān was dwelling in the Heaven of the Pure Abodes, for the sake of the great...
As they were expounding the subtle and wondrous Dharma,
at that time the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī rose from his seat in the midst of the great assembly and bared his right shoulder.
Placing his right knee on the ground and joining his palms toward the Buddha,
he gazed upon the Honored One’s countenance without ever averting his eyes,
and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One."
This great Dharma-gate is profoundly deep, subtle, and truly rare. Nevertheless,
in the future age of the five turbidities,
sentient beings will possess greed, anger, and delusion due to their evil karma.
Deceitful and lacking faith, they delight in practicing what is unrighteous;
they do not cultivate the factors of ethical discipline but are devoted solely to flattery and hypocrisy.
Regarding the power, supernatural faculties, and miraculous manifestations inherent in the dhāraṇī methods, [they lack these].
In all lands, according to their respective locations,
those who seek [this] shall obtain benefit and achieve merit through the ritual procedures for recitation and the methods for sacrificial offerings.
They neither believe nor accept it, nor do they act in accordance with it;
claiming it was not spoken by the Buddha, they slander and revile it, their minds entangled by such evil obstructions.
Consequently, when their lives end, they fall into the great hells.
They undergo extreme suffering with no prospect of escape.
World-Honored One, since these sentient beings have encountered such great misery, how may they be rescued and protected?
We only pray that, out of your compassion, you will deliver them and cause them to emerge [from suffering].
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni extended his hand and stroked the crown of the head of Mañjuśrī, the Dharma Prince,
saying: "Excellent, Mañjuśrī!"
Out of a desire to benefit all sentient beings,
you have been able to inquire of the Tathāgata regarding such meaningful principles.
You should listen attentively and apply your mind with great care.
I shall now explain this dhāraṇī method for you;
it brings peace and happiness to humans and devas, benefits all beings,
and is the most preeminent among all dhāraṇī methods.
This secret and profound [mantra], which accords with the path to enlightenment and relies upon the true *dharmadhātu*, brings forth great merit;
at the time of death, one will certainly be able to remember this King of Mantras of Great Power.
With right mindfulness present, one shall be born in a good realm.
Then he spoke this mantra:

Namaḥ sarvatathāgatebhyaḥ | arhatebhyaḥ | oṃ kumāra-hulubhiṇa viśuddha saṃbhava ajaja ajaja lohulu lohalu balaṃ balaṃ haṃ haṃ śina śi śi mañjuśriye suśriye trailokye sarvaduṣṭabhyaḥ phaṭ phaṭ śamaya śamaya amṛtodvapa udvapa pāpame nāśaya svāhā | Mañjuśrī!
This is your most supreme root treasury of mantras, the Heart-King Divine Spell.
It can eliminate all suffering, afflictions, and calamities;
all evil karmic obstacles shall be completely extinguished.
They shall enjoy longevity, freedom from illness, and inexhaustible wealth and happiness;
their speech shall be eloquent and discerning, and they shall be loved and respected by all people;
furthermore, they shall be able to master and apply all the kings of mantras.
When the Tathāgata Śākyamuni spoke these words,
all the Buddha-fields as well as the mountains, rivers, oceans, and great earth of this world-system,
along with the entire realm of sentient beings, shook in six ways.
All beings in the evil realms— hungry ghosts, animals,
and sentient beings in the hells within the domain of King Yama—
shall have their suffering and affliction stilled and attain peace and happiness.
The Buddha again addressed Mañjuśrī:
"Whether they be devas or humans, men or women,
whether householders or those who have gone forth— among all such classes of sentient beings."
If one can wholeheartedly receive and uphold this King of Mantras,
one shall not be deceived or slandered by evil persons; demons shall find no opportunity,
enemies shall be unable to harm, and poisons shall be unable to injure.
All obstacles and vināyakas shall naturally retreat and disperse.
One who upholds this [mantra] should give rise to this thought:
"The Dharma of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, is inconceivable."
"Only Buddhas and Buddhas can realize and know this.
How could I now dare to give rise to slander?
At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken this Dharma, [remained silent].
That great assembly, together with the Śuddhāvāsa devas,
as well as immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of other devas,
nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, and so forth.
The great ṛṣis who have attained mastery over incantations,
as well as the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī,
the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, and the Bodhisattva Maitreya.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
and other such great bodhisattvas,
as well as the buddha-fields of incalculable worlds.
May all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas together bear witness:
this Great King of Mantras is an inconceivable dharma;
it is a great divine mantra, it is a great illuminating mantra.
This is the unsurpassed mantra; this is the mantra equal to the unequaled.
It can eliminate the obstacles of karmic suffering; it is true and not false.
At that time, the great assembly of devas heard the exposition of the King of Mantras.
All were greatly rejoiced, and they received, honored, and upheld [the teaching].
The Sūtra on the King of Mantras for Eradicating Karmic Obstructions Spoken by the Buddha.
